title: Native Higher-Call Two-Copy SWAP Purity Bridge: Coherent SWAP Excess vs Classical Coincidence Excess, 1-Call Variety Purity Law, and CNOT Autocorrelation Equivalence

theorems.name: Coherent Same-Secret vs Independent-Secret SWAP Identity
theorems.statement: For any k-call schedule (epsilon, sigma), Tr(S_D * E_s[rho(s) tensor rho(s)]) = 1 and Tr(S_D * (rho_bar tensor rho_bar)) = Tr(rho_bar^2), so the two-copy SWAP expectation excess equals the operator Hilbert-Schmidt variance V_HS(epsilon, sigma) = 1 - Tr(rho_bar^2) and the independent-pair antisymmetric projector probability equals V_HS / 2.

theorems.name: Final-Fourier Direction Invariance of Purity and Exact 1-Call Collision Variety Law
theorems.statement: The ensemble purity Tr(rho_bar_(epsilon, sigma)^2) = ||M_hat_(epsilon, sigma)(0)||_F^2 is invariant under flipping sigma_k -> -sigma_k, and for k = 1 it equals |V_(epsilon_1)(f)| / D^2 independently of the error table e.

theorems.name: Exact Harmonic Autocorrelation Law and Two-Copy Coincidence Excess Identity
theorems.statement: Under modular CNOT difference readout Delta = (x_2 - x_1) mod D on two same-secret copies, E_s[P_diff(Delta | s)] = sum_x C(0; x) C(0; x + Delta) + sum_(delta != 0) sum_x C(delta; x) conj(C(delta; x + Delta)), and at Delta = 0 the coincidence excess E_s[P_diff(0 | s)] - sum_x C(0; x)^2 equals E_(epsilon, sigma) <= V_HS(epsilon, sigma).
